definition: A card-sorting test is a neurobehavioral assessment of executive function in which a person sorts cards or card-like images according to changing rules. Performance is judged from patterns such as total errors, repeated use of an old sorting rule, and how many sorting categories are completed, which can help detect reduced mental flexibility or impairment related to brain disorder or damage.
